sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Apple Valley, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Apple Valley lies in northwestern Dakota County, so a sale here involves the county's recording and tax offices in Hastings plus a few city rules on signs, parking and rentals. The paperwork looks much the same whichever way you sell.

The city is mature and mostly built out. Growth slowed after 1990 because the city had virtually used up its buildable land, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 55,248 residents is 2.0 percent below the 2020 count of 56,374.

Owners of homes that need work, carry unpaid tax or have tenants sometimes ask for cash offers, since the buyer accepts the property as it stands. The Dakota County Community Development Agency also coordinates foreclosure assistance and home rehabilitation programs for Apple Valley, which is worth a call before you decide.

sections.h2: How did Apple Valley grow into the city it is today?
sections.html:
The land was first organized in 1859 as Lebanon Township and stayed farmland for almost a century. In the mid-1950s houses began replacing fields, led by the developer Orrin Thompson. Township voters chose incorporation in 1968, and the city incorporated in 1969, picking the name Apple Valley over Lebanon Valley by 1,376 votes to 757.

Growth came fast and then leveled off, as the table shows.

The downtown and the adjacent residential streets, the original core, sit in a shallow valley, and the land around them rolls by a hundred feet or more. The city covers about 17.6 square miles, and Farquar Lake is in the northeast.

sections.h2: What are Apple Valley's roads, schools and landmarks?
sections.html:
Interstate 35E, Cedar Avenue and County Road 42 are the three main routes. The Red Line, a dedicated bus route, links the city with the Mall of America, and the Minnesota Valley Transit Authority runs weekday commuter buses to downtown Minneapolis and Saint Paul. The Minnesota Zoo is in the city, and the Western Service Center of Dakota County is here too.

Independent School District 196 runs the public schools, including a magnet School of Environmental Studies for eleventh and twelfth graders. Families may also choose a school in another district through Minnesota's open enrollment law. The city holds Freedom Days around July 4 and a Winter Carnival in February, and the school district topped the city's 2016 employer list, ahead of Target, Uponor and Dakota County.

The 2020 census counted 21,464 households and 22,253 housing units, 3.5 percent of them vacant. A quarter of households were one person living alone, the median age was 39.4, and 16.6 percent of residents were 65 or older. Later Census Bureau estimates, covering 2020 to 2024, add this picture of owners and renters:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $370,400, with 73.4 percent of homes owner-occupied.
  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $2,084. Median gross rent: $1,738.
  • Households: 21,627, averaging 2.55 people. Median household income: $97,673.
  • Residents in the same home a year before: 88.4 percent.

sections.h2: Which Apple Valley rules should a seller know?
sections.html:
Short term rentals of fewer than 30 days are not allowed in Apple Valley. A council ordinance on June 8, 2023 clarified that they have never been a permitted use, so a house marketed to investors as an Airbnb or Vrbo property will not work as advertised. Owners of any residential rental property must register it with the city.

Yard and curb rules also come up during showings and open houses:

  • One for-sale sign per frontage, two on a corner lot, kept inside the property line and off the right of way, which usually reaches 13 feet behind the curb.
  • Open house signs may stand on city right of way within six blocks of the house, only on the day and during the hours of the open house.
  • Grass and weeds taller than eight inches are a public nuisance.
  • No more than four vehicles per home may be parked or stored outside, and all parking areas must be paved with concrete, asphalt or pavers.
  • Lawn watering is barred from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. between May 1 and September 30, and public sidewalks must be cleared within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.

Sheds of 200 square feet or less need no building permit, and fences over seven feet do. Code Enforcement at 952-953-2570 answers questions, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 handles setbacks.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Dakota County involve?
sections.html:
The county recorder's work sits inside Dakota County Property Taxation and Records, which holds the deeds, mortgages and liens for every parcel. Walk-in recording happens at the Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings, and requires an appointment. Mailed packets need the fees, a cover letter, a return envelope with postage and a phone number.

Land in Minnesota is recorded under two systems. With Abstract property, a title company searches the chain of documents. Torrens property instead carries a single certificate of title, close to final proof of who owns it. Abstract is the norm in Dakota County.

Wells matter at the recorder's counter. A transfer deed, a deed ending a contract for deed included, must come with a well disclosure certificate and a $54 fee unless the deed itself carries a statement. The statement can say the seller is unaware of any wells, or that the wells' number and status are unchanged from the last certificate on file. Staff do not assist with legal forms, so let the title company or an attorney prepare the paperwork.

sections.h2: How do I pay Dakota County property tax from Apple Valley?
sections.html:
Dakota County sets real property tax for May 15 and October 15 and says the owner answers for timely payment, whatever method is used. Manufactured homes follow August 31 and November 16, and farm second halves land on November 16.

Single online payments run through Paymentus. Fees are 2.29 percent on Discover, MasterCard or Visa, $2.95 on the Visa Debit Program and $0.35 on a bank transfer, with a $100,000 ceiling per transaction, and you are done only when an emailed receipt shows up. Alternatives include the phone line at 1-844-797-9075, a mailed check to 1590 Highway 55, Hastings, MN 55033-2343 postmarked by the deadline, or a weekday visit to the Western Service Center in Apple Valley, where a card costs 2.49 percent. The Hastings and West St. Paul offices also accept payments.

Free automatic withdrawals are open to owners without a mortgage-company escrow and without overdue tax; cancellations need 15 days' notice before a due date. Statement and payoff questions go to 651-438-4576 or taxation@co.dakota.mn.us.

faqs.q: Can I run an Airbnb in Apple Valley, MN?
faqs.a: No. Rentals under 30 days are barred, and the council's June 8, 2023 ordinance says they were never allowed. Longer-term rentals must be registered with the city.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for an Apple Valley house?
faqs.a: Property Taxation and Records at the Dakota County Administration Center, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. Appointments are available online, and mail recording is accepted.

faqs.q: What is a well disclosure certificate in Dakota County?
faqs.a: A filing that goes with each transfer deed for $54. A statement on the deed about unknown or unchanged wells can stand in for it.

faqs.q: How many cars can I park outside an Apple Valley home?
faqs.a: No more than four vehicles per dwelling unit, on a paved surface. An annual on-site parking permit allows two more, and the Planning Department at 952-953-2575 takes applications.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Apple Valley?
faqs.a: Independent School District 196. Some families opt into other districts under Minnesota's open enrollment statute.
